title: HOPE ON THE STAGE – The World Is His Stage
story:
On February 28, 2025, j-hope finally returned to the stage as a solo artist. His first solo world tour, HOPE ON THE STAGE, opened in Seoul with three concerts at KSPO Dome. It was the beginning of a journey that would take him across 16 cities and bring together more than half a million fans around the world.

The tour was especially meaningful because it came just a few months after his discharge from military service. After a long time away from performing in front of the fans, j-hope was ready to show the full range of his artistry – and he wanted the concert to feel like a world of his own.

The show was designed as a journey through the different chapters of his musical identity. It opened with the intense sounds of Jack In The Box, featuring songs such as "What if...", "Pandora's Box", "Arson", "STOP", and "MORE". The powerful opening immediately challenged the expectation that a j-hope concert would be only bright and cheerful.

The stage itself was an essential part of the storytelling. Twenty-five movable boxes transformed throughout the show into different settings and structures, reflecting the ideas and emotions behind his music. They became part of the world of Jack In The Box, formed a striking staircase for "MORE", and created the dreamlike space of "Daydream".

The concert then moved through different musical chapters: collaborations from HOPE ON THE STREET VOL.1, his dance-focused solo work, and songs from HOPE WORLD. The setlist also included BTS tracks such as "MIC Drop", "Silver Spoon", and "Dis-ease". Rather than simply performing a collection of songs, j-hope connected the different stages of his career into one continuous story.

And, of course, dance was at the heart of it all. The street dance section brought the audience back to the roots of the artist who had started out as Smile Hoya in Gwangju. The choreography, dance breaks, and interactions with the dancers showed how naturally his musical and dance identities belong together.

The encore was another opportunity to bring j-hope and his fans closer. During "Equal Sign", he wanted to be at eye level with the audience, making the moment feel more personal. The show ended with "NEURON", named after the dance crew that had been part of his life before BTS. It was a tribute to his beginnings and to the people who had helped shape him.

The tour also became the stage for the first live performances of three new solo singles: "Sweet Dreams", "MONA LISA", and "Killin' It Girl". Released during the tour period and later brought together as the Charm of HOPE collection, these songs introduced another exciting chapter in j-hope's musical journey. Each track revealed a different side of his artistry, and his fans had the special opportunity to experience them live as the songs were making their way into the world.

The tour began in Seoul, travelled through North America, Latin America, and Asia, and concluded with two special encore concerts at Goyang Stadium on June 13 and 14. Across 33 reported shows, HOPE ON THE STAGE became the highest-grossing tour by a Korean soloist at the time, with approximately 84.7 million dollars in reported ticket sales and more than 504,000 tickets sold.

For j-hope, this was not just a tour. It was a chance to bring every part of himself to the stage: the dancer, the rapper, the songwriter, the performer, and the artist who had spent years imagining what his own world could look like.

And for his fans, it was a long-awaited reunion – a reminder that no matter how much time passes, the stage is where j-hope and his fans find each other again.

challenge.question: What made the HOPE ON THE STAGE tour especially personal for j-hope?
options: It was his first solo world tour, allowing him to bring together the different sides of his artistic identity.
It was the first time he performed songs written by other BTS members.
It was a tour dedicated exclusively to the music of HOPE WORLD.
challenge.answer: It was his first solo world tour, allowing him to bring together the different sides of his artistic identity.
challenge.explanation: j-hope designed the concert as a journey through his musical career, from his street dance roots to his solo albums and BTS performances. He wanted the show to express the full range of who he is as an artist.
